primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura due to severe ADAMTS13 deficiency
mechanism: Severe ADAMTS13 deficiency prevents normal cleavage of ultra-large von Willebrand factor multimers, allowing highly platelet-adhesive VWF multimers to accumulate on endothelium and form platelet-rich microthrombi that cause thrombocytopenia, microangiopathic hemolysis, and ischemic organ dysfunction.
vignette: A 36-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department for confusion and new petechiae. Laboratory studies show anemia and severe thrombocytopenia. A peripheral smear shows numerous schistocytes. Lactate dehydrogenase is increased, haptoglobin is decreased, and coagulation studies are not prolonged. ADAMTS13 activity is less than 10%.
lead: Which of the following molecular abnormalities most directly causes the microvascular thrombosis in this patient?
correct: Failure to cleave ultra-large von Willebrand factor multimers, causing platelet-rich microthrombus formation
distractors: Failure to regulate alternative-complement activation on endothelial surfaces
Loss of von Willebrand factor binding to factor VIII, accelerating factor VIII clearance
Failure to convert plasminogen to plasmin, producing impaired fibrinolysis
Loss of platelet glycoprotein IIb/IIIa expression, preventing fibrinogen-mediated aggregation
distractor_notes: Uncontrolled alternative-complement activation is a key mechanism of complement-mediated atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome, not severe ADAMTS13-deficient TTP.
Defective VWF-mediated stabilization of factor VIII contributes to bleeding phenotypes such as von Willebrand disease rather than platelet-rich microvascular thrombosis.
Impaired fibrinolysis is not the defining mechanism of TTP; TTP results from failure of ADAMTS13 to process ultra-large VWF multimers.
Loss of platelet glycoprotein IIb/IIIa causes defective platelet aggregation and bleeding, the opposite of the platelet-rich microthrombus formation seen in TTP.
key_expl: ADAMTS13 is the plasma protease that cleaves ultra-large VWF multimers into less platelet-adhesive forms. Severe ADAMTS13 deficiency allows ultra-large VWF to persist on endothelial surfaces, promoting platelet aggregation and platelet-rich microthrombi. These microthrombi consume platelets and mechanically fragment erythrocytes, producing thrombocytopenia and schistocytic microangiopathic hemolytic anemia.
objective: Explain TTP as severe ADAMTS13 deficiency causing persistence of ultra-large VWF multimers and platelet-rich microvascular thrombosis.
